chapter_title: Modification of Interleukin-10 with Mannose-6-Phosphate Groups Yields a Liver-Specific Cytokine with Antifibrotic Activity in Rats
source_pdf: /mnt/project-files/Experimental Provenance for QSAR Dataset/Pharmacology (Luca Gallelli) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).pdf

records.mechanism_rule_name: Mannose 6-Phosphate/Insulin-like Growth Factor II Receptor Agonist
records.role_detail: receptor-binding ligand used as a homing device; the book does not state agonist or antagonist
records.quote: that binds to the M6P/IGF-II receptor which is highly present on activated HSC
records.notes: Role Agonist is an inference to fit the naming rule; the page only says the conjugate binds the receptor (targeting/homing), with no direction of effect. Reviewer may prefer to exclude.

records.role_detail: receptor-binding ligand (uptake); the book does not state agonist or antagonist
records.mechanism_book_wording: M6P-IL10 binds to at least two receptors: the scavenger receptor and the M6P/IGF-II receptor
records.quote: indicates that M6P-IL10 binds to at least two receptors: the scavenger receptor and the M6P/IGF-II receptor
records.notes: Role Agonist is an inference to fit the naming rule; the page states binding only. Binding is deduced in the book from blocking experiments with sucHSA and M6P-HSA.

records.role_detail: possible involvement only; the book does not state a direction
records.mechanism_book_wording: suggests the involvement of yet another receptor, possibly the IL10 receptor
records.quote: suggests the involvement of yet another receptor, possibly the IL10 receptor
records.notes: Speculative statement in the book (uses 'possibly'). Role Agonist is an inference to fit the naming rule (IL10 is a cytokine ligand of its receptor); not stated on the page.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Mannose 6-Phosphate/Insulin-like Growth Factor II Receptor Antagonist
records.role_detail: blocker of the receptor (book calls it a receptor antagonist)
records.quote: or with mannose-6-phosphate-HSA, to block the M6P/IGFII receptor.
records.numbers_detail: dose 5 mg/kg i.v. (PDF page 177); liver uptake of M6P-IL10 reduced from 54 +/- 6% to 24 +/- 8% by M6P-HSA pre-administration (p<0.05) (PDF page 177)
records.notes: Book text on the same page: 'These receptor antagonists (i.v. dose of 5 mg/kg)'. The abbreviation M6PHSA also appears in figure 3 caption (PDF page 177).

records.role_detail: blocker of the receptor (book calls it a receptor antagonist)
records.mechanism_book_wording: succinylated human serum albumin (sucHSA) to block the scavenger receptor
records.quote: succinylated human serum albumin (sucHSA) to block the scavenger receptor
records.numbers_detail: dose 5 mg/kg i.v. (PDF page 177); liver uptake of M6P-IL10 reduced from 54 +/- 6% to 29+/- 4% by sucHSA (p<0.05) (PDF page 177)
records.notes: Printed text reads '29+/- 4%' with a stray space/format as given; 'p<0. 05' printed with a space.

chapter_notes: Skipped 0 statements with targets that are neither receptor nor enzyme. The book never states agonist or antagonist for M6P-IL10 or IL10; Agonist roles are inferred (see notes). Native IL10 is not recorded as an IL10 receptor agonist because no page states that mechanism directly; M6P-modified IL10 is described only as binding or possibly involving receptors.
